Voice of America FAQ

What frequency is Voice of America on?
In the B-26 season Voice of America is scheduled on 79 shortwave frequencies, including 4930, 5860, 5870, 5880, 5940, 6085 kHz. Best evening option for eastern North America: 9420 kHz (8:15 pm – 8:45 pm Eastern). For Europe: 9380 kHz (10 pm – 1 am UTC+1).

What time is Voice of America on shortwave?
Voice of America is scheduled in 43 UTC time windows this season, from 00:00–00:30 UTC through 23:00–24h UTC. English broadcasts: 05:30–07:00 UTC; 12:00–14:00 UTC; 07:00–12:00 UTC; 06:00–06:30 UTC. All times are UTC; subtract your UTC offset for local time.

Can I hear Voice of America in the USA?
It isn't beamed at North America this season, so hearing it in the USA is a DX catch. Your best chance is 9420 kHz (8:15 pm – 8:45 pm Eastern) when that band is open, or listen through an online receiver (KiwiSDR/WebSDR) closer to its target area.

Does Voice of America broadcast in English on shortwave?
Yes. English broadcasts this season: 4930 kHz at 05:30–07:00 UTC to S. Africa; 4930 kHz at 12:00–14:00 UTC to S. Africa; 5860 kHz at 07:00–12:00 UTC to N. Europe; 5940 kHz at 06:00–06:30 UTC to Far East; 6085 kHz at 01:15–01:45 UTC to Far East; plus 31 more.

Is Voice of America on the air right now?
As of Monday, November 9, 2026, 08:33 UTC, Voice of America is scheduled to be broadcasting on 5860 kHz to N. Europe. This is based on the published schedule at the time this page was built; check the live search for up-to-the-minute status.
